a.onclick: openModal( this, "mRNA-vaccine needed time to reach draining LNs", ["39797396"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39797396"], ["PET-CT imaging in rhesus macaques demonstrated rapid trafficking of intramuscularly administered mRNA-LNPs to draining lymph nodes within 4 h."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-vaccine time span to complete LN reactions", ["38161733","37758751"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38161733","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37758751"], ["mRNA and encoded protein were measured at the injection site and lymph nodes after intramuscular administration in NHPs. Lymph-node mRNA was primarily present at approximately 24 h, followed by rapid decline. Tissue sections were evaluated through approximately 7 days, alongside encoded-protein measurements.","Human study: vaccine-specific RNA was detected by RT-qPCR in 8 of 11 axillary lymph-node samples obtained within 30 days, but in none of eight samples obtained more than 30 days after vaccination. However this is not a direct experiment, and mRNA signal could come from non-functional, residual or damaged mRNA."])

openModal( this, "Transient appearance of circulating Tfh cells after vaccination", ["35026152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35026152"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific circulating Tfh cells showed a transient increase in peripheral blood, reaching their maximum frequency approximately 7 days after the second dose. In contrast, spike-specific Tfh cells in the draining axillary lymph nodes remained at relatively stable frequencies for at least 6 months."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-LNP cell infiltration", ["38090568"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38090568"], ["After intramuscular administration, a transient local inflammation drives the recruitment of immune cells that can uptake the mRNA-LNPs and migrate to local lymph nodes."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-LNP vaccine uptake", ["36351374"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36351374"], ["Neutrophils make up a large part of the immune cells infiltrating the sites of injection. Interestingly, neutrophils can efficiently internalize fluorescently labeled iLNPs but show poor production of the encoded reporter protein."])

openModal( this, "mRNA-vaccine expression and cell maturation", ["41169401"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41169401"], ["This response is characterized by rapid activation of dendritic cells, recruitment of monocytes to draining lymph nodes."])
openModal( this, "Early release of type I IFNs", ["40796660"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40796660"], ["Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) are major producers of type I interferon (IFN-I)."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFN inhibits mRNA-vaccine expression", ["41486285","38977924"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41486285","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38977924"], ["Type I interferon restricts mRNA vaccine efficacy through suppression of antigen uptake in cDCs.","The early and intense type I IFN response induced by saRNA detection hinders replication and antigen expression, similar to unmodified mRNA."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFN inhibits mRNA-vaccine expression", ["41486285","38977924"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41486285","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38977924"], ["Type I interferon restricts mRNA vaccine efficacy through suppression of antigen uptake in cDCs.","The early and intense type I IFN response induced by saRNA detection hinders replication and antigen expression, similar to unmodified mRNA."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFN inhibits mRNA-vaccine expression", ["41486285","38977924"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41486285","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38977924"], ["Type I interferon restricts mRNA vaccine efficacy through suppression of antigen uptake in cDCs.","The early and intense type I IFN response induced by saRNA detection hinders replication and antigen expression, similar to unmodified mRNA."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce DC/monocyte maturation", ["28416600"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416600"], ["The critical role of type I interferon (IFNα and IFNβ) in DC maturation and function has been appreciated since the late 1990s."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce DC maturation", ["28416600"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416600"], ["The critical role of type I interferon (IFNα and IFNβ) in DC maturation and function has been appreciated since the late 1990s."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce monocyte maturation", ["40251340"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40251340"], ["IFNβ treatment restored type I IFN responses and proinflammatory cytokine production and induced monocyte maturation."])

openModal( this, "Later release of type I IFNs", ["38777879"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38777879"], ["Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) can produce large amounts of all IFN subtypes during viral infection."])

openModal( this, "Rapid infiltration of type I IFN to draining lymph nodes", ["39191748","38716734"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39191748","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38716734"], ["Injection site-derived IFN-β induces IFN-stimulated migratory dendritic cells that accumulate in the draining lymph nodes and contribute to antigen-specific cellular immunity.","In summary, we observed a transient type I IFN–skewed inflammatory response to mRNA vaccination that was augmented in study participants with prior infection in response to the first vaccine dose."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce CXCL10", ["39312669"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39312669"], ["IP-10 (encoded by the interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) CXCL10) is the molecule most strongly induced by type I and type II IFNs in the whole blood of healthy donors."])

openModal( this, "DCs act as APCs to activate T cells in dLN", ["37708889"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37708889"], ["In cancer patients, dendritic cells (DCs) in tumor-draining lymph nodes can present antigens to naive T cells in ways that break immunological tolerance."])

openModal( this, "Monocytes act as APCs to activate T cells in dLNs", ["36946983","41243288"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36946983","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41243288"], ["These data indicate that even when carefully separated from cDCs, monocytes behave like professional APCs that capture antigens in barriers, migrate to the LLNs, and present to cognate T cells.","Mo-DCs isolated from clinical samples were found to efficiently stimulate naive CD4⁺ T cells in allogeneic assays."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce CXCL10 in dLNs", ["40098954"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40098954"], ["While CXCL10 is originally described as an IFN-γ-induced chemokine, both CXCL10 and CXCL11 responded stronger to IFN-α2a stimulation."])

openModal( this, "CXCL10 recruits T cells to DCs", ["36357313"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36357313"], ["DCs can secrete chemokines that control the spatial organization of T cell responses."])

openModal( this, "Naïve CD4+ T cell priming", ["35026152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35026152"], ["Our current results provide strong and direct evidence that a high-magnitude, antigen-specific CD4+ T cell response in the draining lymph nodes."])

openModal( this, "High antigen-specific CD4+ T cell response", ["34252919"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34252919"], ["BNT162b2 vaccination resulted in the robust production of neutralizing antibodies against the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 (derived from 2019-nCOV/USA_WA1/2020) and, to a lesser extent, the B.1.351 strain, as well as significant increases in antigen-specific polyfunctional CD4 and CD8 T cells after the second dose."])

openModal( this, "Naïve CD8+ T cell priming", ["41986715"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41986715"], ["Here we report that mRNA–LNP vaccines do not require cDC1 cells or the WDFY4-dependent cross-presentation pathway for CD8+ T cell priming but instead engage both cDC1 and cDC2 cells redundantly."])

openModal( this, "Modest antigen-specific CD8+ T cell response", ["36630611"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36630611"], ["Spike-specific CD8⁺ and CD4⁺ T-cell responses increased modestly after monovalent and bivalent mRNA boosting."])
openModal( this, "Antigen-specific Th1 differentiation", ["32998157"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32998157"], ["Most participants had T helper type 1 (TH1)-skewed T cell immune responses."])

openModal( this, "Antigen-specific CD4+ T cells produce IFNg", ["36146571"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36146571"], ["At Day 14 after boosting, S1-specific IFN-γ-producing CD4+ T-cells showed a two-fold increase compared to baseline after the full dose intramuscular booster (IM full dose)."])

openModal( this, "Antigen-specific CTL differentiation", ["33627851"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33627851"], ["Effector T cells leave the lymph nodes armed with specialized functional attributes."])

openModal( this, "CXCL9 induces Th1 differentiation", ["41813655"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41813655"], ["These chemokines are primarily produced by monocytes, macrophages, endothelial cells, cancer cells, and fibroblasts in response to interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and TNF-α. All three selectively bind the chemokine receptor CXCR3."])

openModal( this, "High presence of Th1 in blood serum after vaccine", ["34252919"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34252919"], ["Consistent with previous studies, the CD4 T cell responses were primarily of the T-helper-1 type, although there was a low-level T-helper-2 (IL-4) response. IFNγ and TNF were the dominant responses in CD8 T cells; three individuals with no known exposure to SARS-CoV-2 responded even at baseline, suggestive of CD8 T cells that are cross-reactive to related viruses, as has previously been shown."])

openModal( this, "High presence of CTL in blood serum after vaccine", ["34320609"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34320609"], ["We detected a rapid and substantial induction of spike-specific CD8+ T cells that were present in 9 out of 13 tested donors already at days 6–8 and peaked in most donors 9–12 days post prime."])

openModal( this, "Differentiation of Tfh cells", ["38001088"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38001088"], ["Follicular helper T (Tfh) cells are essential for the formation of high affinity antibodies after vaccination or infection."])

openModal( this, "FDCs mostly originate from MRCs", ["35332263"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35332263"], ["Computational single-cell transcriptomic trajectory analysis of human lymph-node stromal cells identified a continuous differentiation path through marginal reticular cells and terminating in follicular dendritic cells, supporting MRCs as a likely precursor state for FDC development."])

openModal( this, "Naïve B cell priming", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Germinal centres (GC) are lymphoid structures where B cells acquire affinity-enhancing somatic hypermutations (SHM), with surviving clones differentiating into memory B cells (MBCs) and long-lived bone marrow plasma cells."])

openModal( this, "GC Tfh cell differentiation", ["37330549"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37330549"], ["Studies have shown that dendritic cells are sufficient to prime naïve CD4+ T cells to generate PD-1+CXCR5+Bcl6+ cells9, which then require interactions with B cells to become PD-1hiCXCR5hiBcl6hi GC-Tfh cells."])

openModal( this, "B-cell somatic hypermutation", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination, spike-specific B-cell clones persisted in draining lymph-node germinal centres and progressively accumulated somatic mutations in their immunoglobulin genes; somatic hypermutation frequencies in spike-specific GC B cells increased approximately 3.5-fold over six months."])

openModal( this, "B-cell receptor affinity selection by FDCs", ["30504208"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30504208"], ["Human germinal-centre B cells bearing higher-affinity BCRs form more stable contacts with membrane-associated antigen and internalize antigen more efficiently, establishing an affinity threshold for positive selection."])

openModal( this, "B-cell receptor affinity selection by Tfh cells", ["35026152","35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35026152","https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination, spike-specific Tfh cells persisted in human draining lymph nodes, and their abundance correlated with the magnitude of the spike-specific germinal-centre B-cell response.","Following BNT162b2 vaccination, spike-specific Tfh cells persisted in human draining lymph nodes and correlated with spike-binding GC B-cell responses; continued germinal-centre maturation generated increasingly mutated B-cell clones and antibodies with improved affinity."])

openModal( this, "Few high-affinity receptors kept in GC to proliferate", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination, spike-specific germinal-centre B-cell clones persisted and evolved for at least six months, accumulating somatic mutations associated with increased antibody affinity and avidity."])

openModal( this, "Germinal-centre B-cell differentiation into plasma cells", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Germinal centre-driven maturation of B cell response to mRNA vaccination. Selected germinal-centre B cells differentiate into memory B cells and plasma cells. Following human mRNA vaccination, spike-specific germinal-centre B-cell clones were clonally related to lymph-node and bone-marrow plasma cells, supporting the differentiation of selected GC B cells into affinity-matured antibody-secreting cells."])

openModal( this, "Germinal-centre B-cell differentiation into memory B cells", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Persistent germinal-centre responses following human mRNA vaccination generate somatically mutated, antigen-specific memory B-cell clones."])

openModal( this, "Failure of positive selection leads to centrocyte apoptosis", ["34925321"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34925321"], ["Human germinal-centre B cells require sufficient affinity-dependent antigen acquisition and Tfh-derived survival signals for positive selection; light-zone B cells that fail to obtain adequate help remain apoptosis-prone."])

openModal( this, "Appearance of circulating Tfh cells after mRNA vaccination", ["35026152"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35026152"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific circulating Tfh cells transiently peaked in blood after the second dose, while spike-specific Tfh cells persisted in vaccine-draining lymph nodes."])

openModal( this, "Plasma cells transient increased levels in blood", ["34182569"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34182569"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific IgG- and IgA-secreting plasmablasts peaked in blood one week after the second dose and subsequently declined, becoming undetectable three weeks later."])

openModal( this, "Memory B cells increased levels in blood", ["34648302"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34648302"], ["Following two doses of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine, spike- and RBD-specific memory B cells were detected in the blood of all previously uninfected participants."])

openModal( this, "Human FDCs express CXCL13", ["34424268"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34424268"], ["Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses of human tonsillar stromal cells identified CXCL13 as a highly expressed defining gene of FDCs, supporting their role in maintaining the CXCL13 gradient that organizes B-cell follicles and attracts CXCR5-expressing B cells and follicular T cells."])

openModal( this, "Transient increase in circulating CXCL13 after mRNA booster vaccination", ["38090597"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38090597"], ["This clinical study measured serum cytokines and chemokines in COVID-19–naive people receiving repeated BNT162b2 vaccination. A transient systemic increase in CXCL13 was detected after the third dose, supporting the presence of increased follicular or germinal-centre-associated activity after booster vaccination."])

openModal( this, "Vaccine-specific plasma cells seed the bone marrow", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Following human mRNA vaccination, spike-specific IgG-secreting plasma cells were detected in bone marrow and were clonally related to vaccine-induced germinal-centre B-cell populations."])

openModal( this, "Bone-marrow plasma cells secrete vaccine-specific antibodies into circulation", ["35168246"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35168246"], ["Six months after BNT162b2 vaccination, spike-specific IgG-secreting plasma cells were detected in human bone marrow, and their affinity maturation was associated with enhanced anti-spike antibody avidity in blood."])
openModal( this, "cTfh1 cells produce IFNg", ["27231124"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27231124"], ["Activated CXCR3⁺ circulating Tfh cells produce IFN-γ."])

openModal( this, "cTfh1 differentiation to long-lived memory cells", ["35314848"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35314848"], ["Recall of vaccine-induced spike-specific CD4 T-cell memory was associated with transient CXCR3 expression and expansion of activated circulating Tfh cells."])

openModal( this, "CD4+ T cells surviving to memory", ["34726470"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34726470"], ["A subset of vaccine-induced CD4⁺ T cells survives contraction and forms memory. Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific CD4⁺ T cells expanded and subsequently contracted, while a persistent population with central-memory, effector-memory and stem-cell-like memory characteristics remained detectable for at least six months."])

openModal( this, "Contraction of the antigen-specific CD4⁺ T-cell response", ["34726470"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34726470"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific CD4⁺ T cells expanded after immunization and subsequently declined during the physiological contraction phase, while a persistent antigen-specific memory population remained detectable for at least six months."])

openModal( this, "CD4+ memory T cells produce IFNg", ["35764089"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35764089"], ["Spike-specific memory CD4⁺ T cells produce IFN-γ upon antigen recall. Following mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific memory CD4⁺ T cells-including cells capable of producing IFN-γ after ex vivo antigen stimulation—remained detectable for at least six months."])

openModal( this, "CD4+ T cells migration driven by chemokines", ["33912186"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33912186"], ["Activated human CD4⁺ T cells upregulated CXCR3 and migrated toward CXCL10-containing chemokine signals; neutralization of CXCL10 significantly reduced their migration, supporting CXCL10–CXCR3-dependent recruitment."])

openModal( this, "Spike-specific CD4⁺ T cells produce IFN-γ after mRNA vaccination", ["34044428"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34044428"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific CD4⁺ T cells displayed a Th1-polarized response and produced IFN-γ and/or IL-2 after ex vivo antigen stimulation, with responses remaining detectable for at least nine weeks after the booster dose."])

openModal( this, "Vaccine-specific CD8⁺ T cells produce IFN-γ after antigen stimulation", ["34044428"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34044428"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific CD8⁺ T cells produced IFN-γ and/or IL-2 after ex vivo antigen stimulation, demonstrating a vaccine-induced cellular immune response that persisted for at least nine weeks after the booster dose."])

openModal( this, "A subset of vaccine-induced CD8⁺ T cells persists as memory cells", ["35839774"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35839774"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific stem cell-like memory CD8⁺ T cells emerged early after immunization, and their frequency was associated with the durability of the antigen-specific CD8⁺ T-cell response six months later."])

openModal( this, "CD8+ T cells undergoing cell contraction", ["34726470"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34726470"], ["Following BNT162b2 vaccination in humans, spike-specific CD8⁺ T cells expanded after immunization and subsequently declined from their early peak, while a smaller population with memory and stem-cell-like memory characteristics persisted for at least six months."])

openModal( this, "CD8+ memory T cells produce IFNg", ["35941157"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35941157"], ["Following COVID-19 mRNA vaccination in humans, a stable population of spike-specific memory CD8⁺ T cells persisted for several months and retained the capacity to expand and produce IFN-γ and TNF following in vitro peptide restimulation."])

openModal( this, "CD8+ T cells migration driven by chemokines", ["34320609"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34320609"], ["Human CXCL9- and CXCL10-containing chemokine signals recruit CD8⁺ T cells, while BNT162b2 vaccination rapidly induces and mobilizes spike-specific CD8⁺ T cells in humans; direct CXCR3-dependent trafficking of the vaccine-specific cells has not been demonstrated."])
openModal( this, "CXCL10 recluting CD8+ T cells", ["39190494"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39190494"], ["CXCL10 contributes to recruitment of CD8⁺ T cells."])

openModal( this, "CXCL11 recruits CXCR3⁺ CD8⁺ T cells", ["39302156"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39302156"], ["In a human intestinal organoid model, epithelial CXCL11 promoted the migration of primary human CD8⁺ T cells; neutralizing CXCL11 significantly reduced their recruitment, supporting CXCL11-dependent trafficking of CXCR3-expressing CD8⁺ T cells."])

openModal( this, "CXCL10 recruits activated CXCR3⁺ CD4⁺ T cells", ["33912186"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33912186"], ["Activated human CD4⁺ T cells upregulated CXCR3 and migrated toward CXCL10-containing signals; neutralization of CXCL10 significantly reduced their migration, supporting CXCL10–CXCR3-dependent recruitment."])

openModal( this, "CXCL11 recluting CD4+ T cells", ["29207310"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29207310"], ["The CXCL9, -10, -11/CXCR3 axis has been a major focus of research, since it regulates differentiation of naive T cells to T helper 1 (Th1) cells and leads migration of immune cells to their focal sites."])

openModal( this, "Type I IFNs induce CXCL11", ["38716734"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38716734"], ["We found that, within the infection-experienced cohort, preexisting levels of spike-specific CD4 memory T cells and spike-specific memory B cells were significantly correlated to the fold change of several proinflammatory cytokines, notably the IFN-inducible cytokines CXCL10 and CXCL11, at 24 hours after the first vaccine dose."])

openModal( this, "CXCL13 directs B-cell localization and follicular organization", ["37202489"], ["https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37202489"], ["Single-cell and spatial analyses of human lymph nodes and tonsils identified CXCL13-expressing reticular cell networks underlying B-cell follicles, supporting their role in recruiting and organizing B cells within follicular niches."])
